## ⛔ The one file this card must not touch, and it is the one the card points at

The card's evidence table comes from `packages/runtime/src/http-metrics-inbound-coverage.hono.integration.test.ts`. **That file is on sibling card #9650's branch and is being actively edited right now** — #9650's ruled fix must flip two of its assertions.

⇒ ⛔ **Do not edit, extend, or add cases to that harness.** Read it if useful; ⛔ never write to it. If you conclude this card genuinely needs a change there, **STOP and report** — the two cards would then need sequencing, which is my call, not a widening you may take.

⚠️ Triage ruled explicitly that **no `Blocked-by:` is wired**: the comment correction does not depend on #9650's branch landing. So ⛔ do not wait on it either. Both halves of that instruction matter — don't block, don't touch.

## What is actually wrong, and what "fixed" means

The guard is **installed correctly today**; there is ⛔ no live defect and ⛔ nothing to change about its behaviour. What is false is the stated *rationale* — the part the next author copies:

> …as long as the middleware is added before `kernel:listening` fires, it intercepts every request regardless of which plugin registered its handler.

Measured false: every route mounts in Phase 2 `start()`, and `kernel:ready` / `kernel:bootstrapped` / `kernel:listening` all fire *after* Phase 2. A middleware installed from a `kernel:bootstrapped` hook — which satisfies the comment's stated condition — observes **nothing**. **The sufficient condition is Phase 1 `init()`**, which is what the code does and what the sentence should say.

Triage's scope: name Phase 1 / `init()` as the requirement, and **drop the "order-independent for matching" clause**, which is the specific phrase that makes the false generalisation sound principled.

⭐ Why this is worth a card at all: the guard is a **refusal surface**. Anything modelled on this comment that installs from a lifecycle hook ships a guard that gates nothing — no error, no log. The comment is the defect's delivery mechanism.

## Premise-first

Re-read the comment block on current `origin/main` before writing. ⚠️ The card cites `:3429-3435`, but `serve.ts` moves constantly and a sibling measurement already put the guard's install near `:3464` — ⛔ **do not trust the line numbers**; locate the block by its text. If the comment has already been corrected or removed, `premise_still_valid: false` with no PR is the right delivery.

Also verify the two-phase claim yourself on the current ref rather than inheriting it (`LiteKernel.bootstrap`, `ObjectKernel.bootstrap`, and where `kernel:listening` is emitted relative to Phase 2). The correction's whole value is that the replacement sentence is **true**; a comment fix that ships a second false rationale is worse than the first.

## The optional assertion — your call, on measurement

Triage left "an assertion that the install happened during init" to the dev. Take it only if you can make it assert the real property cheaply and locally in `packages/cli`. ⚠️ If it would require the `packages/runtime` harness, the answer is **no** (see the boundary above) — ship the comment correction alone and say why.

## Gates

Re-derive with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` from the **actually changed** paths. ⚠️ Known gap, twice-measured: it names neither `pnpm lint` nor `check:slot-lookup` — run `pnpm lint` regardless. A comment-only diff to a published package's `src/**` still needs a changeset judgment call: state your reasoning either way rather than assuming `skip-changeset`.

Read verdicts from reported counts, ⛔ never a piped exit code. Report at draft-PR time — ⛔ do not wait on CI convergence. Terminal report: machine-checkable fields only.

## ACCEPT — PR #9821

`domain:cli` seat, session `session_01WeN7F6jQFpcqW2BN56RdPa`, round 23. Reviewer of record; checked against GitHub and the tree, ⛔ not against the report's self-description. ⏳ Landing gated on CI — see bottom.

### Checklist

- **Form** — draft ✅ · base `main` ✅ · `Fixes #9745` ✅ (the PR discharges the card whole) · 2 files, 99+/4- · labels carry `skip-changeset`.
- **Scope** — `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` + `packages/cli/src/commands/serve-unknown-hostname-guard.test.ts`. Both in `packages/cli`; ⛔ no governed path ⇒ no ACCEPT fork, this seat may land it. The widening beyond `serve.ts` to the guard's own test file is within the "an init-time assertion beside the guard" clause of the brief and was declared, ⛔ not silent.
- **⛔ Hard boundary HELD.** `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD -- packages/runtime/` is **empty** — sibling #9650's harness was read and never written, exactly as instructed. This was the single most likely way this card could have gone wrong, since its own evidence table points readers straight at that file.
- **`Blocked-by:`** — correctly none, per triage. ⛔ Neither wired nor waited on; both halves of that instruction honoured.

### The claims I verified rather than accepted

**① Is the replacement sentence actually TRUE?** That is this card's entire value, and a second false rationale would be worse than the first. Every factual claim in the new comment checks out on `origin/main`:

| claim | reading |
|---|---|
| `createConsoleStaticPlugin` mounts the Console in `start()` | ✅ `packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts` — `init: async () => {}` is **empty**; `start:` is what calls `getRawApp()` |
| both kernels run every `init()` before the first `start()` | ✅ `LiteKernel.bootstrap` (`lite-kernel.ts:55`), `ObjectKernel.bootstrap` (`kernel.ts:312`) |
| the "order-independent for matching" clause is dropped | ✅ gone — that was triage's named scope, and it is the phrase that made the false generalisation sound principled |

**② The new pin is the real thing, not a green rubber stamp.** It registers `/before` **ahead of** the guard's `init()` and `/after` **behind** it on **one** `HonoHttpServer`, drives the same unmapped hostname at both, and asserts `asked === ['nobody.objectos.ai']`.

⭐ That last assertion is the part that makes it a measurement: the registry being consulted **exactly once** is direct evidence the `/before` hit never reached the guard — which is what separates *"the guard didn't run"* from *"the guard never installed"*. The test's own header names that failure mode and says why neither direction can be satisfied by a middleware that simply never installs. It also states plainly that every **other** test in the file mounts the guard first via `mountGuard` — i.e. the case that works — so ⛔ none of them could have caught the false claim coming back. That is an honest account of why a new test was needed at all.

Reverse verification is targeted, ⛔ not a template: moving `/before`'s registration after `init()` flips `200 → 404` at a named line (`Tests 1 failed | 34 passed`), restored → `35 passed`. The no-rebuild statement is reasoned from the import specifier rather than asserted.

**③ The changeset judgment — and a wrong suspicion of mine, corrected.** The dev applied `skip-changeset` and cited #9802 as precedent for "prose-only inside a published `src/**`". `packages/lint/src/runtime.ts` shows **+66** lines in that commit, which looks nothing like prose, so I went to overturn the citation.

⚠️ **I was wrong and the citation is sound.** Filtering that diff to non-comment lines returns **empty** — every changed line begins `*` / `//` / `/*`. #9802 carries `skip-changeset`, and it verified its own claim the hard way: hashing `dist/*` before and after showed **exactly two published files changed, both sourcemaps**, no `.js`/`.cjs`/`.d.ts`.

⭐ The raw line count is what misled me — *read the hit, do not count it*, collected on me for the second time in this shift. Recording it because a reviewer's rejected objection is as much a reading as an accepted one.

Independently: `packages/cli/tsconfig.build.json` carries `"exclude": ["src/**/*.test.ts", "src/**/*.spec.ts", "src/**/__tests__/**"]` ✅, so the new test cannot reach the published tarball. `Check Changeset` is green. The judgment stands on its own reasoning even without the precedent.

### Deviations

⛔ None. Scope, boundary and triage's no-`Blocked-by:` instruction all honoured; `check:type-check-coverage` / `-debt` were declared **not run locally with the measurement that justifies it** (the package's `tsconfig.json` includes `src`, so the new test already sits in a tsc program; no TEST_DEBT entry to move) rather than silently skipped.

### ⏳ Landing — ⛔ not yet

Six required checks read by name (⛔ never an aggregate): `Build Core` **success**; `Test Core` 2/3 and 3/3 **success**, 1/3 **`in_progress`**; `Dogfood Regression Gate` all three shards **`in_progress`**; `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Temporal Conformance` **`in_progress`**. ⇒ Stays draft; flip-ready then enqueue on convergence.
